utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case Number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Stamp, you started to examine the witness Mr. Fazlic yesterday. I think we could resume.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Usher, could you please bring in the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Fazlic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: From your answer, I do understand that you can hear me in a language you understand. You were only here for a short time yesterday in the courtroom. Counsel for the Prosecution will now continue to examine you as a witness. Mr. Stamp, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You said last time, yesterday, that you started to referee a football game from about 10.00 in the morning on the 1st of June, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, the game that you refereed, how many players were there on the pitch, approximately, or exactly, if you know?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can tell you accurately. There were 12 teams of five players in each. Each team had five players, so five would be playing against five. So one match would involve ten players.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. I take it all the players were males?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, young men, 18, 17, 16, up to 20 years of age.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can you say if these young men were in the army or not?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me be quite frank with you; it is normal for some of them to have been in the army, but he was not on duty, he was on leave, so that is quite normal, but many of them were not in the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now you said at about 10 to 20 minutes after the game started, something happened.

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the left-hand side there was a corner, next to the goal. And all the players went to the left side of the pitch to make the penalty kick, so I moved a metre to the left of the pitch, enable to watch, and I bent down. We carried out the penalty kick, and just as we were doing that, a shell fell among three players; a young man called Dragan and another young man. Then I too was hit by shrapnel, and I saw immediately that there were 11 young men on the ground. Only the goalman, on the right, was not injured. And behind the goal, to the right, another young man was lying down. So eight players were on the ground and three others who were not playing were on the ground. I was the only one who remained standing among them. I was all covered in blood.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Where did that shell fall in relation to that area of the pitch where the corner kick was being taken?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The pitch, as I said yesterday, was about 15 to 20 metres wide and about 40 metres long, so the middle would be about 20 metres, so half the pitch would be a square. And the shell fell some 20 centimetres to the left of the centre. Right in the centre of the pitch, right in the centre, to the left, 20 centimetres to the left, and the spot has been marked.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: How has that spot been marked?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The spot was marked with brown varnish. The spot is about 10 centimetres in diameter, and in fact, the whole pitch was marked with a stripe 10 centimetres wide. It is brown varnish used for metal.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's take this very slowly now. You remained standing after the shell fell. Did you notice anything in respect to the spectators who were in the vicinity of the pitch where the corner kick was being taken?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were a lot of children on these overturned cars. These cars had been turned over ever since the 4 or 5th of April 1992, and they were standing there. There were about 40 cars that had been destroyed on that parking lot, and we lined them up to prevent the ball from getting away. And the children were on these cars, and they all fell on their backs, all the children. I thought that a lot of children had got killed; however, it so happened that 82 or 83 were wounded, some of them lightly, some of them more seriously, and eight were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: What happened to you after the shell fell? Did you feel anything?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I took a step towards the passageway and the building, and I couldn't move any further and I fell. There was blood gushing out from five places; my upper leg, lower leg, all over my stomach, and my spine. My whole left side was totally damaged. My skin was in a terrible state and I couldn't move. I was lying in a pool of blood that was gushing out from me.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, before you fell, did you observe anything else? May I rephrase that.

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: What did you observe?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I saw three of my players totally dismembered, their legs and arms. It was only their track suit that held them together, and I saw, on the right, the citizens were planting onions there, and a lot of people were on the ground there, people I knew who were behind the goal. And I saw a young man under a car who was already dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the first shell.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Was there any other shelling at that time?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Three or four seconds later, after the first shell, a second shell fell. But it missed the vehicles and fell some 10 metres behind the vehicles that we had used for protection. And a young man was hit. His leg was injured. The shell fell in front of him and broke off his leg.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: When this second shell which fell about three to four seconds after the first shell fell, were you standing or had you yet fallen?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember exactly, because there was panic, and I thought another one would fall.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. How far from the first shell did the second shell land?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, about 12 to 14 metres away, roughly. I didn't measure it. If the pitch was 15 metres wide, half is 7, so then behind the vehicles, that would make it 15 or 16. I can't tell you exactly. But you have the video that I myself made, and you can look at it, if you like.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, we'll do that in a moment. Now, were you taken to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. 16 were killed on the spot, and 82 were wounded, some lightly, some more seriously. Some wounded children ran home, thinking that they could -- their parents would treat their wounds, and they were wrong. An infection set in. And as there was no fuel and no vehicles for transportation -- you know what Dobrinja was like. If you don't, I can explain it to you if you ask me. There were only three vehicles available, and there were 82 of us. Some were on the boots of the cars; some were on the roofs, on the engines, on the gear box, so that people were running alongside, holding us so we didn't fall. And Jusuf Hajir, who was in charge of the hospital, sent us to the state hospital that used to be a military hospital, and then he divided us in half. Some went to the Kosevo Hospital, and others to another hospital so that we were distributed among three hospitals in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I see. Now which one did you go to?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I first arrived at the Dobrinja hospital, and they saw me, that I had been badly hurt. Then they transferred me to the former military hospital. They just gave me a drip and treatment for shock, and then I was transferred to the university clinic at Kosevo where I was immediately treated.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: How long did you remain at the Kosevo Hospital?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stayed 56 days, or rather, about two months. I was wounded in both legs. I couldn't move for 50 days. I couldn't get out of bed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Tell us, if you can - you should be able to - what was the nature of your injuries and whether or not you have any lasting physical effects as a result of the injuries.

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The injuries were dangerous. One affected my right foot, my right foot was cut off by part of the shell. Another one hit the bones of the left foot. Then I was hit 25 centimetres, close to the anus [as interpreted] of my upper leg. One hit me in the neck, and also in the spine. One shrapnel hit my lungs, one in the eye, so that I see double. And there was superficial injuries in the stomach. There were numerous, numerous fragments. Maybe thousands, because I was only three and a half metres away from where the shell landed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And have you any lasting consequences from the injuries?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do suffer consequences. The shell must have been a magnetic shell. I still have some shrapnel in my body, and I developed serious infection twice. Then my pancreas has been affected. After that, I developed asthma. Then my left eye, I see double; and I have a piece of shrapnel in my tongue which makes breathing and talking difficult.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: What's the condition of your legs now?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of my wounds is still open and is -- still open so that I'm unable to do anything, though I'm 57 years old, and the injury in my leg has still not healed fully.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Which leg is that?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The foot of my right leg, my right foot is swollen.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, did you recover from the hospital a medical certificate in respect to your injuries and treatment?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I immediately received a certificate. You have it with you, the discharge document from the Kosevo clinic. And I didn't bring the documents from the Dobrinja hospital, whereas I was bandaged for three months after that under the most difficult conditions and under sniping. I went during the winter when the land was covered with snow and ice, and people would drive me there, as they could, though there was a sniper on the church.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Which church is this?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the Serbian orthodox church, a newly-built one, and the facade had not yet been completed. And up the scaffolding, anyone could climb, and it is only 400 or 500 metres away from this football pitch. And the church steeple could easily be climbed upon because of the scaffolding.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The church from which the sniping came, was it under the control of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina or was it under the control of the army of the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you yesterday that the separation line held by the Serbs and the BH army was along Indira Gandhi Street, the Partizanskih Olimpijada, across the bridge, next to the school, and this church was about 100, 150 metres away from the separation line on the Serbian side.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: With your leave, Mr. President, Your Honours, may I have the witness look at the document marked P1197.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And English translation is P1197.1.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Is that document you have in front of you a copy of the discharge paper that you received from the Kosevo Hospital?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Just look at the date of birth. It says 1941 but it's wrong; it should be 1945. The date of birth, 1945, not 1941. And on page 4, everything else is identical with the documents that I have, and other documents that I have in my possession. And the last document, Fazlic Ismet, again, instead of 1941, it should say 1945. I was born in Vogosca. My parents lived in Sokolac, so nobody came to Sokolac for four years. In 1940, 1941, and 1992, my family has been forced to leave their estate. You can look and inquire the condition in which those houses are, the houses of my parents which they had to abandon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, just to mention, this witness has a document made of four pages in the original language, and we only have three pages in the original language. There is a fourth page missing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have only received three pages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I had some difficulties in following any reference to page 4 as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, I was just about to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could I, Mr. Usher, have that document which he has. Thank you. Mr. Usher, could you put the document on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Witness, could you put away any other document that you have and photograph that you have. Please have a look at the document to your right, and could you just point out for the Court what you referred to as page 4. What did you refer to as page 4? Could you let us know, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I think the error arose from the fact that he was presented the document along with the translation, and he is pointing to the first page of the translation as page 4, and which explains this same error which he refers to on the first page of the B/C/S copy in respect to the date of his birth being the similar mistake on the first page of the translated copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Usher. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, the places where these two shells impacted, has anything been done at those sites?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Two years ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: One moment. Could you put away your photograph, please. Put it away.

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Two years ago, from the municipality of Novi Grad, people came to indicate the spot and the places where people were wounded. And I personally showed these people where the two shells had landed, not only myself but it was a few of us. There was 10 or 20 people of us who had been injured, wounded. We came along to tell them where the shells had landed. We call the area Sapa where it landed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The impact sites where the shells landed, were there any craters or damage caused to the asphalt of the parking lot where the shells landed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Terribly sorry to interrupt. I have not heard the place, the name of the place. We would like to verify it on the map. Maybe this witness could tell us, if he remembers. What is the last word he just said, so that we can follow on the map? The last name of the site that he just mentioned, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You mean the word? It's Sapa.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that clear enough for you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, the last answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, personally I'm not too certain. My colleague will probably be able to find it. I can see if it's written here on the map. No, it is not clear. Unfortunately, we cannot find it on the map. Could the witness please spell the name or repeat it clearly so we can know what he is talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat it slowly, the name you just gave us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can call that area Sapa, where the shells landed, we call it Sapa. It's S-A-P-A. It's the impact site where the shell hit the asphalt right in front of me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much for repeating your answer. Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That impact site where the shell hit the pavement in front of you, and other impact site where the shell fell some 15 metres away caused damage to the pavement, I take it. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we can see very clearly the trace on the pavement of all the shells and shrapnel that had hit the pavement. The pavement is a hard area, it's a hard -- it's hard and the shrapnel was able to get through, and they had damaged the asphalt. Four to five centimetres deep was the damage, and as soon as the shrapnel hit the pavement, they would then ricochet. So on the side where I was standing, the pavement was scratched more whereas on the other side, the side opposite of where I was standing, we can see that the pavement was scratched at only a few places because the shrapnel had just ricocheted very quickly, and they fell off -- fell away.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm terribly sorry, Mr. President, but this is very important for us to establish whether this witness talked about the sidewalk. I'm not too sure if he talked about a sidewalk. Maybe we can ask him the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but Mr. Piletta-Zanin, of course, if there's any clarification needed, you can do that during cross-examination. It's not the way we usually deal with these kind of -- of course, if there's something which is totally unclear for everyone, you could interfere. But otherwise, Mr. Stamp may examine the witness. If there's anything unclear, you can clarify it during cross-examination. That's the usual way. I'll allow you now -- well, you've asked it, so I'll ask Mr. Stamp whether he could ask clarification from the witness. But usually, if there's anything unclear, it's during cross-examination that you're able to clarify with the witness what is --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. President, for this observation. But by doing this, I am only abiding by one of the instructions of your Chamber. You have asked me to intervene as soon as there is an interpretation problem, and in French I heard "trottoir." I did not wish to interrupt the witness in order not to break the rhythm of my colleague. I asked for the end of the intervention. I wanted to be honest by waiting, but next time I will intervene immediately as Mr. Stamp is asking questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If it is a matter of interpretation, please indicate so that it's quite clear to me that we have a language problem rather than a problem of the content of the testimony. So whenever you think there's a problem related to translation or interpretation, please make that clear so that we know exactly what we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is the reason of my intervention. I did not wish to bother anybody inside this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, you noticed what the problem of Mr. Piletta-Zanin was. Could you please try to find out whether there's any misunderstanding or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President. As it pleases you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You were speaking about the two shells that fell on the 1st of June, 1993. Did any of them fall on a sidewalk?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, please. If we're talking about asphalt on a parking lot, if we call that a sidewalk, well, I don't know what this gentleman is thinking of. Sidewalks are made out of concrete --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. Fazlic, could you just, for the sake of economy of time, just let us know if any of the two shells that you are speaking of fell on a sidewalk or did they fall on the playing -- on the car park surface?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, must I really explain to you how wide the parking lot is? I've already explained where the shells fell. The parking lot is wide, 15 metres wide, and it is 14 metres long, and the shells landed right in the middle. So it's seven and a half metres away from the sidewalk, so seven and a half metres from the sidewalk fell the first shell, and 24 metres away was the impact site of the second shell. It is very clear, you cannot discuss it. A sidewalk is the end. It's 80 by 100. That parking lot is made of the -- there are sidewalks all around it. If you want to talk about pavement or asphalt, asphalt is the surface that covered the parking lot. We can even see it today, it's very clear on the pictures. You can have it here. There are no problems here. So both shells fell on the asphalt of the parking lot. On the asphalt of the parking lot, not on the sidewalk.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Fazlic. Now, you just waved a picture. Is that your photograph?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: For the time being, we're not going to use it. Could you please put it away.

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thanks very much. Now, the two shells, you said, caused some damage to the impact site where they landed. Have those areas where those two shells which fell on the 1st of June, 1994 -- 1993, I beg your pardon, been preserved in any way?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: How?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are some red substance that has poured into the -- that was poured into the holes that were left by the shells. So this is how we marked the spots.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, in that parking lot, are there other marks from other shelling?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's not only one trace, but 1.100 spots that were left on that parking lot. Different calibres of various shells, mortars. I'm not a specialist, I cannot tell you what calibres there were exactly, but I know that I would bring cars in that parking lot before -- I was actually putting out fire on the cars that were in the parking lot, cars that were set on fire, they smelled bad, and those were holes in the asphalt, and so the asphalt was damaged.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I take it from your answer that that parking lot had been mortared, or shells from mortars had fallen there on other occasions. Were these occasions before or after the 1st of June, 1993, or both before and after the 1st of June, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please. At the very beginning of the war -- I'm not talking about aggression, the aggression or anything like that. I did not say those words. I will never say these words. May the experts call it the way they will. But from the very beginning, the shelling of Dobrinja - and I'm only talking about the Dobrinja neighbourhood, please. I'm not talking to you about Sarajevo because I did not go to Sarajevo. I was not in Sarajevo. I was only in Dobrinja. There was not one single day where one or two or three shells didn't land, either in the corner of the parking lot -- but you can see our dressing rooms only 15 metres away from the parking lot. There was a tank in from Lukavica, from the barracks, in all the four -- the heating plant was damaged. And it happened that they missed it and then the shell damaged four apartments and the corner of the building -- the apartment building was not at the front line, it was not where the battles took place. It was directly fired from Lukavica in a straight line from a -- from a tank. And the parking was shelled with mortars --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Fazlic, if I may interrupt you. I'm fully aware that you'd like to tell the whole story of everything you experienced. I hope, on the other hand, that you'll understand that in this courtroom, we hear a lot of witnesses. One is telling us about a specific moment; another one is telling us about other moments, or some are telling us about the whole period of time. I think the Prosecution has called you specifically in relation to what you experienced at this football match. So since we have to use our time as efficiently as possible, I'd ask you to respond to all the questions by Mr. Stamp, or later on by counsel for the Defence, and leave it to counsel on what are the most relevant issues to be discussed with you. Not because I do not understand that you would tell us perhaps for hours all you know, but since in this courtroom we have to find a way of getting in the information in such a way that this trial will not take seven years. Would you please answer specifically on the questions of Mr. Stamp. And I think his last question was whether there had been any mortars or shells landed before or after the day of the football match on that same parking lot.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Before and after.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, in respect to those other marks caused by those other mortars which landed, were they preserved by the same red thing which was poured into those two which landed on the 1st of June, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Those shells that had fell left an impact mark, and they can still be seen today. They did not injure anybody, just the cars. They just hit the cars that were overturned, and there was a fire. The cars were set on fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, do you recall in September -- I beg your pardon. In the year September 2001, showing OTP investigator Barry Hogan and Commandant Hamill the two impact sites from the 1st of June, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And those are the two impact sites in the parking lot which had been marked with red, or with a red substance?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And did you point out for OTP investigator Barry Hogan certain positions on that parking lot where the incident happened?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And this was done -- and this was recorded on a videotape?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: With your leave, Mr. President, I'd ask that videotape P3281B be played.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Leave is granted, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: "THE INVESTIGATOR ON TAPE: Could you please show me, by standing on the spot, where one of the posts -- goalposts was located on the 1st of June, 1993. "THE WITNESS: [Indicates] "THE INVESTIGATOR ON TAPE: Would you now please show me, by standing on the spot, where the second goalpost at this end of the parking lot was located on the 1st of June, 1993, to the best of your recollection. "THE WITNESS: [Indicates] "THE INVESTIGATOR ON TAPE: Could you now please show me, by walking to the spot and standing where the goal was located at the other end of the playing field, to the best of your recollection, on 1st of June, 1993. "THE WITNESS: [Indicates] "THE INVESTIGATOR ON TAPE: I will mark this spot with an X with yellow paint with the number '1' beside it. "Could you now please show me, by standing on the spot, where the second goalpost for the goal at this end of the playing field was located, to the best of your recollection, on the 1st of June, 1993. "THE WITNESS: [Indicates] "THE INVESTIGATOR ON TAPE: I will mark this spot with yellow paint in a figure X with the number '2' beside it. "Could you now please show me, by standing on the spot where, to the best of your recollection, you were standing on the 1st of June, 1993, when the first shell exploded. "THE WITNESS: [Indicates] "THE INVESTIGATOR ON TAPE: I will now mark this spot with a yellow X in yellow paint, with the number '3' beside it. "Could you now please show me, by standing on the spot where, to the best of your recollection, the first shell exploded on the 1st of June, 1993. "THE WITNESS: [Indicates] "THE INVESTIGATOR ON TAPE: Mr. Fazlic, could you now please show me, by standing on the spot and indicating with your hand, the outer limit of the playing field which was lined with wrecked cars, to the best of your recollection, on the 1st of June, 1993. "THE WITNESS: [Indicates] "THE INVESTIGATOR ON TAPE: Once again, could you please stand on the spot and indicate with your hand as you stand on the spot. "THE WITNESS: [Indicates] "THE INVESTIGATOR ON TAPE: I will now draw a line along this plane with yellow spray paint. "Could you now please show me, by standing on the spot, where, to the best of your recollection, the second shell exploded on the 1st of June, 1993. "THE WITNESS: [Indicates] "THE INVESTIGATOR ON TAPE: Mr. Fazlic, one final instruction, please: Could you please walk to the other end of the playing field and indicate the corner where the line of old cars came together, to the best of your recollection, on the 1st of June, 1993. "THE WITNESS: [Indicates] "THE INVESTIGATOR ON TAPE: I will now mark this location with yellow paint in a line along this plane. And along this plane. Thank you very much."

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. Fazlic, the places that you indicated on that videotape, were those indications made to the best of your ability and recollection?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Because I measured the playing ground, and I painted it with paint, with brown varnish, the day before.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: With your leave, Mr. President, may I also show the witness a photograph?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it's a 360-degree photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes. And that is P3672A. I'm sorry, P3678A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the number that appears on my list as well. I just repeat that the Defence opposes against the use of this type of 360-degree photographs. The Chamber is aware of that. Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Could it be moved a little bit to the right. Thank you. Stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: There are some hills there to the background in that photograph. What's the name of those hills?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That hill is called Mojmilo. It starts from the municipal water supply system to the Lalovic houses. That hill is where the municipal water supply is, and where the transporters for the water were.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And in relation to the football pitch, in which direction is that hill?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One could say it was to the north of the football pitch, and on three sides are six-storey buildings. And I think that this hill is to the north.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. So this -- may I just phrase it as a question. Under whose control was this hill in June 1993; which party to the conflict?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This hill was virtually no man's land. Up here, there's a forest, and there was a sniper, a VBR, operating along this meadow so that nobody could move around, but it was under the control of the army of BH.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you move the photograph to the right, please. Stop there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And is this one of the blocks of the -- one of the blocks of apartment buildings which was on one side of the car park?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You can see the nylon cover, that is my apartment. And this was the passage for civilians going to Dobrinja. It's called 3B. The steps were made subsequently, and the handrail. In front was a shell that made this big damage at the beginning of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you move that to the right slowly, please. Stop there, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: In the background, there's another apartment block, and this would have been on the -- another side of the car park. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the apartment building forming a 90-degree corner, and this passage leads to the square where a tank and a sniper from Dobrinja IV were active, so this was completely shut off with boards, wooden boards.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, in the foreground of this photograph, there is a semi-circle with a chain linked around that semi-circle. Could you describe what that is?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was a welder, working for the central heating, so I made these bars and tied a chain to them to mark an area that vehicles could not park in. And we wanted this area to be marked and a monument to be built, and this is a monument marking where this happened. Actually, it happened in front, but as it's a parking area, we couldn't put it on the exact spot. It still exists to the day, and fresh flowers are put there regularly and I can show you a photograph of what it looks like.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you move the photograph to the right a bit more, please. And stop there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And those are the apartments to the -- well, which direction is that?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: So that I don't lead him at his answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can you say which direction are we looking into now? Can you say?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are looking from the position where I was wounded towards the west. Where the white vehicle is parked, there is another passage. This is the second passage that the people of Dobrinja used because they wouldn't dare go to the right because there was a tank, and a sniper, and along Kasindolska Street, no, not Kasindolska, Lukavica Street to Nedzarici, there was protection there out of overturned vehicles, but there was a passage that we could use.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you go a little bit to the right, please. Stop there, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You pointed out already Mojmilo hill. Now we're to the left of that first place we stopped at. There is a tower in the centre of the photograph, towards the background. What is that tower?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll explain for you. This is our central heating plant, for central heating. And it was hit with several projectiles from a tank. Everything was destroyed, and that white dot that you see in the white area -- four times this tower was targeted but it couldn't be overturned because it is made out of one piece.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you very much. Now, within this area bordered by these three apartment blocks, are there any military facilities, to your knowledge, or were there any military facilities in June 1993?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not here. To the front and towards the east, towards Lukavica, over here, towards Lukavica, yes. The front lines. There were military facilities, and we had no access there. We needed to have passes from the ABiH. Each one of us needed to have a pass. I've kept this pass, to be able to move around. I could show it to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm really sorry, but I think that the witness said in his mother tongue, which is Serbian - Ms. Pilipovic will correct me - that he spoke of the first lines rather than the front lines. I think that the distinction is important because neither the English translation nor the French interpretation mentioned this. So could the witness repeat what he said, and I think it is rather important that we get it correctly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Fazlic, when asked whether there were any military facilities within the area bordered by the three apartment blocks, you said "Not here, but..." What did you then exactly say? Did you say to the first lines, to the front lines, or...?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said in front, yes. And that means as we're looking at this picture, so towards us, the separation line was there between the BH army and the Serb army. The Indira Gandhi Street and the Partizanskih Olimpijada are two parallel streets leading towards the River Dobrinja. One street is used by a bus going to the school in Dobrinja I. It is 8 metres wide and it has two green surfaces, and that is where the separation line was. There were military facilities there, and the military zone was there, and we were not allowed access to that area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you're talking about separation or front lines and not about first line or second line or third line. You referred to separation lines -- line, yes. Does that clarify?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness used, and we can hear the tape if necessary -- just a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, to have a clarification, which I think is useful for the discovery of the truth, could the witness simply say whether he used in his mother tongue the expression "the first lines," because that is what we heard a moment ago, and we can verify on the tape, whether a moment ago he used the word "first lines," yes or no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, it's not a normal way to do it, but since I do not speak any B/C/S: Mr. Fazlic, the Defence would like to know whether you used in your answer a certain word in your own language. That word will now be spoken by Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Could you please then confirm whether you used that expression or did not use that expression. Would you please give the expression.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Pilipovic will tell us what is the expression used by the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Pilipovic will give an expression. Could you please confirm whether you used that expression in your answer or not. Please, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Thank you. Mr. Fazlic, in answer to a question from my learned friend, did you say that you were unable to go to the "first front line" that you had no access to the "first lines"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, without permission. Everything is clear now. Yes, without permission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Witness, I'm asking about the enclosure, that enclosure which is surrounded on three sides by three blocks of apartments, do you know of any military facilities being in that area in June 1993?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I can list all the military facilities and tell you exactly where they were, if you wish.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'm quite sure we'll get to that. Thank you. Now, can you say about how large this parking lot in total is, approximately?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see the parking is marked on this picture. One parking area is 220. So the whole area is 80 by 110 metres. And there's a guard here next to the heating plant. Look at that. And then I know exactly, it's 80 by 110, 112 metres. And there are four such parking areas in a line.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I take it your answer is that the size of the parking lot is about 80 by 110, 112 metres. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's so. Judging by the vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. And on the south side of the parking lot, there's a grassy area, a lawn which goes towards the apartment block to the south. Would you like to refer to the photograph again? Please turn to the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I must object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have the impression that one is asserting that this or that is to be found in this or that direction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please rephrase.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The question is in the form of a statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Witness, please have a look at the photograph again.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Please turn the photograph to the right again. It's P3678A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you have any technical difficulties in moving it? At least, your case manager --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, please move it to the right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Stop there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You said that was north? Earlier you said the hills in the background, Mojmilo, was towards the north?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have a compass to be able to tell you exactly, but judging by the sun, where it rises, I think this is to the north, towards Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Please turn to the right. Stop there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: This set of apartments which borders the parking area would be to which direction if the hills are to the north?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the east, if I'm standing here where I was wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Okay. Please turn it approximately 90 degrees. Go on, turn it to the right 90 degrees. Stop there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That area of apartment blocks --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to find my way, Mr. President. We are told that we would be turning roughly 90 degrees, and personally I'm not sure that this corresponds to 90 degrees. But it is merely an observation so that we can find our way in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. Fazlic, that area of apartment blocks, can you say approximately which direction it is from the car park?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is south. You see, the grassy area with the children's playground. Before the war, there was a slide and a playground for children.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, that is a grassy area I'm referring to. From the edge of the car park, the apartment building, about how far it is from there to the apartment block?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Approximately what is the distance from the edge of the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There's a fire brigade path here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There are three blocks of apartments on the photograph, so that we know exactly what we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, it took us now one and a half minute to get to a grassy area which, as far as I can imagine, even my wildest imagination, could not be in dispute. You objected because the question was leading. As you know, usually the parties are allowed to lead the witness especially when there is a matter which is not in dispute. On this picture, I think there can be no doubt as to whether there's a grassy area at that part of the parking lot. We're looking now to an apartment block. We went there slowly, going from one apartment block to another apartment block. I'm afraid that this is clear to everyone, perhaps not to you. But I think if it's so clear, that it's up to you to make it clear for yourself. Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I allowed Mr. Stamp to proceed at this very moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. Fazlic, could you just tell us approximately what is the distance in metres, if you can, just tell us how many metres, approximately, it is from the edge of the apartment -- from the edge of the car park to the apartment block to the south of the car park.

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you please listen to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I will --

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can count the distance. There are 46 or 48 metres from the edge of the monument to the fire brigade path, which is only 4 metres from these buildings. From this corner where this vehicle is, right around the buildings. So this is a new neighbourhood. A fire brigade path was built, and no vehicle is allowed to pass. Children can play there, and there are all kinds of games for them. It has now been repaired --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Fazlic, may --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These are my flowers here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would be able to give a specific answer on a very specific question. The question was about the distance. If you know about the distance, tell us. If you have difficulties in assessing it, tell us that it's difficult for you. But you give a lot of other information which I'm certainly aware is very important in your view, but we leave it usually to counsel to point at the issues that are most relevant at that moment. Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I take it that the distance between the edge of the car park to the apartment building to the south is about 52 metres?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. 46 is the grassy area, two and a half metres is the fire brigade path, and then 4 metres to the building. Is that that important?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, very well.

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Too many questions. I'm not an expert to measure. I should have measured the whole of Dobrinja and give you the measurements. And I would if I could walk.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, may I ask you at the same time how much time you would still approximately need. If it's just a matter of a couple of minutes --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: It's a matter of maybe two or three questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You don't know how many minutes that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: It would be probably two minutes, but I wonder, if it is not inconvenient, if we take the break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps if we could finish the examination-in-chief in a couple of minutes, we'll do that and it's more natural to have the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The crowd was gathered in the small corner of the car park which you showed us on the video.

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. People gathered.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And the two shells fell within 15 to 20 metres from each other where the crowd was gathered. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And I take it you said that they were just a matter of 3 to 4 seconds apart.

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Roughly.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you say if, to your knowledge, or if you have any information which could assist us, whether or not persons on the other side of the confrontation line would have been aware that you were having a football tournament that morning?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yesterday, at the end, I told you that we were protected on four sides, and it was not possible with binoculars to discover what was going on. They couldn't know, as far as the first lines and the soldiers on duty on the first lines are concerned. Now whether someone else knew where this particular part of the parking area was where we were playing, if a shell had fallen, it could have landed on the green surface, the heating plant or anywhere else instead of amongst us. So it means that someone after all must have known that there would be a match, because an evening before that, a shell fell only 10 metres behind the playground, or rather, to the north of that playground. And I showed the gentleman the spot. It has been marked, too. And then the next day in the morning, it was quiet, a beautiful day. We came out. We made a mistake. That was our destiny. We knew. There was an order from the army that not more than three men should gather in one place because they would be hit. That is how they could hit Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. our children.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. You said a shell fell the night before, in the parking lot. Do you know if it was a mortar shell or any other type of shell? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same, the same calibre, the same holes, the same sounds. That was a test.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: How -- I beg your pardon. You said the same holes. The mark left by the shell which fell the night before, was it similar to the mark left by the shells which fell on the 1st of June, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Nothing further, Mr. President, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Stamp. Mr. Fazlic, we'll have a break now for half an hour. And upon resuming, it's counsel for the Defence that will put questions to you. So we'll adjourn until 5 minutes past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, is the Defence ready to cross-examine the -- it will be Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence is ready. I shall be conducting the cross-examination. May I proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Witness.

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you for coming back in this courtroom. The Defence is at your service. We know very well that it is incredibly painful for you to be here after having been hit by these thousands of shrapnels that you mentioned earlier. I saw that you have pictures with you, or a picture. Would you be able, please, to take it out to show it to us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, may I ask you, is it your intention to tender anything in evidence, or is this a photograph you know what is on it?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I do not know at all what this picture represents, but I know that this witness knows things. So rather than clipping his wings and stopping him from saying what he wishes to say, why do not we let him show us evidence, pictures, and I believe that maybe the witness may explain to us --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, if you do not know what is on the photograph, at least you should ask the witness about what type of photograph is in his hands, what is on this photograph, in order to find out whether this could be relevant evidence or not. We'll not allow any of the parties, nor the Defence nor the Prosecution, to just say, well, tell me what you've got there, show it on the ELMO, and we'll see whether it will be of any help. On the other hand, if there is relevant material in the possession of the witness, then of course we could ask whether the witness is willing to give it to the Defence. I mean, you have got nothing at this very moment in your hands which you could offer as evidence. So first, try and see whether you will be in a position to offer anything in evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you, Mr. President. But I thought that the witness in his own language said that he had his -- he had himself taken pictures of the parking lot and the precise spot where the incident occurred. If I misunderstood, the witness will tell me, but this is what I thought I heard. And therefore the pictures in front of him represent - this is only, of course, a logical inference of the Defence - but those pictures represent probably the parking lot.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Is that so, Witness? Yes or no, please.

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This picture is the monument erected at the spot where the crime happened. I brought it because I want you to see it, and I want my children to see it. I hope that this will never happen to anybody; not in New York, not in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir. We will put the picture on the screen later on, if you will allow us. However, I will begin with asking you some questions. I will first ask you some military questions. Do you know Mr. Hadzic? Do you know Mr. Hadzic?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Sir, do you know if Mr. Hadzic was a high-ranking military representative?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was not a military person before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for this answer. Thank you. Witness, tell us, this high-ranking official, was he a commander of a brigade in Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, I said before the war he was not a military man. He had another profession.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: But I'm talking about the period during the war.

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a brigadier.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of the 5th Motorised Brigade in Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: What was his rank, please? Could you give it to us, if you know? Was he a general, a colonel, for instance?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said he was a brigadier. It is a rank of a lieutenant colonel, former lieutenant colonel.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I will interrupt you right now. You said "brigadier. " If I interrupted you, it's because I hear the interpretation in another language, and I heard, in the French language, "sergeant." So he was not a sergeant but a commander of this brigade. Is that so, Witness?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If a commander of a brigade is a brigadier, then he was a brigadier. He was a commander of a brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You are perfectly right, and I thank you for this precision. Now, Witness, would you be able to tell us, what was his designation? I'm sorry, what was the designation of this brigade? Was it the 1st, 2nd, 3rd?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just told you that it was the 5th Motorised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. I do not believe I heard you if you said how many men are in a brigade.

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not a military expert. If you would have asked me for the former JNA, I would have been able to tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Would you please answer. If you know the situation for the former system, you may give me the answer then, please.

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Three to four battalions, if you know what a battalion is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, thank you. I do understand, but unfortunately, not everything, as I am told. Can you, therefore, since you know what the situation is, can you tell us with precision how many men are in a battalion?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, please. I was a tank driver of the T-55 tank, and I served my military service in the JNA. I was a T-55 tank driver. I could not tell you how many men are in a battalion. I can give you an approximation. I can tell you a hundred, 200 to 300 but I'm not too sure. Do not ask me these questions. Those are superfluous words for me. I am not a historian, I am not a military expert.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Terribly sorry, Witness. But please do understand that I do not know everything that you know so that is why I must ask you some questions. Very well. Now, do you know if in Dobrinja there were some barracks where people, men, belonging to this brigade were stationed?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Dobrinja, there were no barracks, but atomic shelters. These men -- no, they are four atomic shelters. In Dobrinja IIIA, IIIB in Dobrinja, because it is a new construction. They have built atomic shelters that can hide 3.000 people, approximately. And in those atomic shelters were the headquarters of the armies and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I will interrupt the witness here. I think we have some interpretation problems. The witness just said, and my colleague knows -- my colleague Ms. Pilipovic knows what the problem is. I do not see it in the transcript. But it is a minor, perhaps, language problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I'm asking you the following question because I did not go there, I do not know. But in other words, were there barracks built outside and not in basements? Were there facilities, buildings with walls where soldiers were stationed, so therefore outside?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible that those were dormitories for the soldiers, whereas the command post was in Dobrinja II and the offices were there as well. With regards to the atomic shelters, this is where all the other types were stationed. It is possible that some may have slept in some apartment --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you for your answer. When you tell us that the soldiers were in those shelters, you are talking, referring to apartment buildings. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I told you that Dobrinja is a new construction built under the new conception. And each Dobrinja has -- each part of Dobrinja has atomic shelters, and there are three atomic shelters, and they did not allow us to use, us civilians, those atomic shelters. We remained in basements, in trenches, in the worst possible installations whereas they took the atomic shelters.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you for your answer. Now, we're talking about atomic shelters. We also have some in our country. Those are shelters that are built under apartment buildings. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. These shelters are built on the square. There are four buildings in the shape of a V. And right in the centre, there's a shelter, so that you have one, two, and three shelters along the same line, and the length of it is two kilometres. It's like an avenue.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Well, when you're talking about a square, are you talking about a square covered with asphalt?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The square was not -- did not have an asphalt surface. The square is about a metre to a metre and a half above the asphalt and above the street level, and I'm talking about the shelter. The shelter is elevated. So there's a ground level, it's a metre and a half from the ground level, and it's approximately, long, 40 to 45 metres in length. And inside, in its inside, the ground, where today you have various shops.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Witness, am I understanding you well, did you say that the army was stationed between those apartment buildings but in these basements, and those were fortified basements?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In that atomic shelter, or rather, on that square, because the atomic shelter does not reach the apartment buildings. It's in a V. It's in the shape of a V. There are four buildings, and right in the centre there's the atomic shelter. 40 times 45, the length is 45 metres, and then there's the entrance and you have a generator for the air, and this is what it looked like.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Civil Protection members know what it was. I understand. But for now what I wanted to visualise is the following: These shelters were situated between each group of apartment buildings, in order to service those apartment buildings? Is that so?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did say there were three atomic shelters, in Dobrinja IV under Serb control, one in Dobrinja IIIB and one in Dobrinja IIIA, and they're one after the other in the same line, and those are three squares.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You said that the 5th Motorised Brigade was there. Would you be able to give us the name of the street where the command post of this brigade was, therefore, of the 5th Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just for Dobrinja II.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Witness, do you have an idea of the street name where the headquarters were?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please do not ask me this question, because there are so many streets in Dobrinja. Right now, I cannot remember, believe me. You are tiring me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I'm terribly sorry to interrupt you. When you're telling me not to ask you this question, are you telling me that you cannot remember, or are you telling me that you do not wish to answer my question? I understand both versions. I understand you, but please tell us which one it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, if you would have listened to not only the first part of the answer but also the second one, it becomes clear to you that the witness said, "Don't ask me because I don't remember."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The streets names have changed, and I cannot remember. In Sarajevo, all the street names changed, and I cannot find myself any more, I cannot orient myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, if I allowed myself to ask this question it's because we know that the street names changed, and the witness just confirmed this. But I was thinking that maybe he could remember the old name of the street. It might be an important element before your Chamber. Witness said do not ask me this question, but you may ask me this question later because I may remember it, and this was the doctor that was responsible for the Dobrinja clinic, and this is the reason why I'm asking this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... the witness whether he would know the old or the new name, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I understand that you do not remember any more the old names. You don't know the new names, you don't remember the old names, but if I give you a map, if I showed you a map, would you be able to visualise on the map where the headquarters were located?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is this really very important for you?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes, it is. It is. It has an exceptional importance for you, for us, and for everybody in this courtroom. I believe that it is, and I believe that we are all in search of the truth. Would you be able to tell us where the headquarters were situated, were located, please?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For Dobrinja II, across the street from the pharmacy and the post office. That's all I can tell you. Whereas for the street name and for the number, I can't tell you. My street used to be called Vahide Maglaic, and now it's called Trg Djece Dobrinje, so believe me, there's no point.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. I really sincerely thank you for this answer because I know that, after being wounded, I know personally that it is not easy to be objective. Now, if I showed you a map, would you be able to show us the PTT building and the streets where you lived?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I would not want to interfere in the style of questioning of my friend. He makes comments during the course of asking questions which may or may not be proper, and I don't interfere or interrupt just because of the comments. I just interrupt because this particular comment is a reference to the objectivity of the witness, and it is not a proper comment to be made at this stage of the case, if at all. May it please you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I think it's improper to thank the witness for the answer, and then adding that you know that after being wounded, you personally know that it's not easy to be objective, because it's a comment on the objectivity of the answer. We hear the answers. The quality of the answers will be assessed by the Chamber later on and is not needed at this moment during the examination of the witness of any comment. Of course, during final argument, you may give whatever comment you'd like on the quality of the answers of the witnesses, on the objectivity or not, but no commenting during the examination of the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Mr. President. I must admit --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- I shouldn't have made any comments. This came spontaneously.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, if I were to show you a map, could you point out in Dobrinja where the post office was that you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, the President of the Court told me not to talk about other things except about the match. I have come to testify about the match, and not to tell you where the command was, who was in command and what they did. I was a civilian, and if you're interested, you have a commander, Sefer Halilovic, and ask him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Fazlic, please, there is a misunderstanding. I indicated that the Prosecution called you mainly because of what you know about the match. Therefore, I asked you to answer the questions put to you by the counsel for the Prosecution and not to give all kind of perhaps even important information but not asked for by counsel. Now we are in a situation that counsel for the Defence asks you specific questions, and if you have any doubt on whether you should answer these questions, ask me. But please not start any debate with counsel for the Defence. And would you please answer the question whether you would be able to indicate on a map where the post office in Dobrinja was. Would you be able to do so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I won't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're not able or you're not willing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not willing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Fazlic, the rules in this Court are such that if you are able to indicate on a map where the post office in Dobrinja was, that you should do so. May I remind you of this obligation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Show me the map. If I can I will. And if I can't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your cooperation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Show me the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, present a map to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have the usual map that we usually produce. I don't know whether we have a clean one, Madam Registrar, or whether you wish us to give the witness this one. We have a sufficient number of copies, but it is the same map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... marked a copy, yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As it will probably be marked, Mr. President, it is better to give him a clean copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. You have in front of you a map, and with the assistance of the usher, it is on your right. Don't write anything on it for the time being, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Fazlic, could you perhaps first put the map on the ELMO. The usher will assist you. And please listen carefully to Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, you have this map. Do you recognise it, which is in front of you?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't see. Well, if I could have it in front of me, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I'll give you another copy which I have here, with the assistance of the usher, please. We know this map more or less by heart, but I would be grateful, Witness, if you would be kind enough not to write anything on this map. Did you hear me? Don't write anything, please. Put the pen down. I'll tell you in a moment why. Put the pen down. Thank you very much. Witness, do you recognise the map in front of you?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it a map on which you can see the area known as Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, still without writing anything, tell me, is that a map on which you could recognise the position of the parking lot where the incident occurred? Let me remind you that it was close to the Lukavica road, which I think is marked on the map.

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Next to the Lukavica Road.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About -- next to 349. That is where the parking lot is. No, 333. 33, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, is this a map on which, like me, you can see a sign roughly in the middle of the map, the middle of Dobrinja, which corresponds to the emblem of a post office in the form of an envelope? Do you see that sign in the middle of the map, next to the numbers 348, I think it is? Witness, for technical reasons, will you please speak out your answer. If it's no, say no; if it's yes, say yes. Did you say yes?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Fazlic, I saw that you are nodding.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you don't speak aloud, nodding will not appear in the transcript of this Court. So therefore, if you're nodding --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: This sign that you have seen is the post office that you mentioned a moment ago, or is it another post office?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So it is indeed the post office opposite which was the command post?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Witness, could you please tell us if, close to this post office, is the Dobrinja hospital?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Across the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. Witness, I'm now going to ask you to do the following: As you have localised these points, could you, on this same map, indicate the places where the anti-atomic shelters were that you mentioned a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Next to number 401, and 406 would be the second one. Those are two atomic shelters in Dobrinja IIIB. An under number 33 is the parking lot where I was injured.
