utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, thank you for that. I'm now going to ask you to do the following: The usher, who is on your right, is going to give you a pen, a marker, a black marker.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [In English] Mr. Usher, would you try to find a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, could you please assist me. I have no difficulties in finding 406, but could you guide me to 401.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, in order to assist everyone, what I would like to do is the following, and that is to ask the witness, who has found these places, to put the map on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, do you hear me?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you please turn to your right, if you can -- if you have any difficulty, the usher will assist you in doing so -- and will you look now at the same map but which is placed under the ELMO. Do you recognise the same map, that it is the same map as the one you looked at a moment ago?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, with the pen, a black pen that will be given to you, will you mark a circle around the post office. A small circle, please.

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Fine. Could you put number 1 next to that circle, please.

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Fine. Witness, you said that across the road was the command post of the 5th Brigade. Could you mark that with a second circle, please.

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. So will you put a number 2 next to this dot so that we are able to find it later on.

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Fine. Thank you. Witness, would you please, also on this map, mark the position of the Dobrinja hospital, which you said was across the way.

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, you've drawn a line. Would you please put 3 under this line so that we are able to find these places.

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness. Witness, still on this map, if you could, of course, could you please indicate the group of buildings where the atomic shelters were. And if you could, you could just mark those places with crosses.

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll mark the atomic shelters with crosses.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes, quite.

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You've marked two crosses, and you mentioned several shelters a moment ago during your testimony, Witness. Was the other shelter on another territory?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was one in Dobrinja IV, and I don't know in Dobrinja V, there were garages and shelters.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could you mark those garages with a cross.

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Up here, I think it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Make a cross again, please, following the same logic.

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This shelter is under Serb control -- it was under Serb control, you see.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: It doesn't matter. It doesn't matter, Witness. Just put a cross.

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I'm not so familiar with Dobrinja IV.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: We have taken note of that. Witness, still on this same map, in response to some questions from the Prosecution, you mentioned the existence of first lines. Could you, on this map, indicate where those first lines were, perhaps with a dotted line so that we can see it on the screen. Have you understood my question, please, Witness?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have, and I can. And on from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness. We're now going to leave the map to the side. We'll come back to it, so you can put down your pen, but we leave the map on the screen as we will certainly need it a little later, if the President and the Chamber allows more questions about the map. Anyway, thank you for the information you have given. Along this same line of questioning, Witness, we come to the concept of military police. Witness, do you know who was in charge of the military police during the war, at the time of the war?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were several of them. They changed, so I don't know them, believe me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: If I give you the name of Mr. Karem Mucarevic [phoen], is that a name you know?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: This person, Witness, was he, at a certain point in time, in charge of the military police, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but he was replaced.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The name is Lucarevic, "L" like "Leon," for the benefit of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, with respect to this military police, did you know whether this police at a certain point occupied the hill that you pointed out as being the Mojmilo hill?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: When you say, "No," Witness, does that mean that you don't know or that you know that they did not occupy the hill?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do know, and the answer is no.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: As you know that they did not, do you know then where the headquarters of the military police were situated?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, is it because you no longer know the name of the street, or could you please indicate in relation to certain facilities like the hospital, the post office, or some other prominent buildings? Or do you simply don't know anything about it?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know, really, about the military police. About the civilian police, yes; but the military, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Tell us, then, please where the civilian police was, if you can, on this map. If you need to write anything, do so to your right, on the map to your right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [In English] Mr. Usher, would you give a black pen to the witness so that he could write it down. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, will you please make a little circle. Have you done that?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And add the number 4, I think it is.

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. So you've written the number 4 next to this dot. Witness, as we're on the map now, and to avoid tiring you, could you, with a triangle this time, mark the parking area where this incident unfortunately occurred.

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You have marked a V. You have written a V, I think. I can't see it too well. Could you please close this V and make it into a triangle. I don't see that you've done that. Make it a triangle.

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That's perfect. Thank you very much, Witness, for these indications. I should now like to ask you another series of questions. We will leave the map aside, and I thank the usher for his assistance. So we leave it there. We may be coming back to it. Witness, I'm referring to your professional training. We know that you were a specialist for central heating. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm a highly-skilled worker for central heating, and I have 30 years of experience behind me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. Was it in this capacity that you worked in the service known as the Civil Defence?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I apologise. May I say something?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was offered a weapon, but no, I said, I will never kill. I have never killed. I refuse to pick up arms, and I reported to the Civil Defence simply to do good work, peacetime work, of which I am proud. But I would never carry a weapon and kill people. I had a chance to carry a weapon, and I went for interrogation twice on that score.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for your clear position. I can't comment on it, but I wish you to know that I heard the message. When we're talking about Civil Defence, would you please tell us, what were the first and the second lines? A moment ago, you spoke about the first defence line, and I will later come to another question about the second defence line. Could you tell us, as far as you know, what was the first front line?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but I marked it for you with a dotted line on the map. Look at the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the first defence line.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Fine. So the first line is the line where elements of the army were stationed in the strict sense of the word. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on both sides. Dobrinja IV was the Serb side, and Dobrinja IIIB on the Bosnian side. They were separated by a street eight metres wide and two grassy areas six metres wide each.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much for that clarification. Witness, if the first defence line is the line that is strictly military, what was the second defence line?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, the witness testified about the first defence line. It is my recollection that he was talking about the first line, but whether this was the first defence line or not -- or would you please clarify this, but otherwise, please indicate where he talked about the first defence line.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, a moment ago, you talked of first lines. Were you talking about first defence lines?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, let us understand each other clearly. What I marked on this map, on the one side and on the other side of the street is a row of buildings, Indira Gandhi Street, and that's on the Serbian side. And Partizanskih Olimpijada is on the other side, under numbers 1, 5, 7, 9 and 11 on the Bosnian side. In those buildings, there were no civilians at all. Those buildings were only and solely under the army of the Bosnian BH. Those buildings were completely pierced through. They were turned towards Dobrinja IV, and the walls were completely filled with holes whereas at the other side, on the Indira Gandhi side, those buildings were turned towards Dobrinja III. This is where the nests --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Fazlic, may I just ask you for a clarification. If you're talking about the first line, do you refer to the line held by the army of the BiH, and would then the second line be the line held by the Serbian forces? Or would there be a second line after the first, also held by the Bosnian -- the BiH forces? Would there be one line for each party or would there be more lines on the BiH side?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe we didn't understand each other perfectly well here. Regarding the BiH army, there was one first line. With regards to the Serbian line, there was a first line, only one line, and the only thing that separated the two was one street. So the BiH army and the Serbian army, they each had only first lines and it's along one road, one street. There were no second, third, 14th, 15th line. Do you understand me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I fully understand you. Thank you for your clarification. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Mr. President. Thank you very much for your intervention, and I will just try to make some precisions, if you allow me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, when my learned friend from the Prosecution was putting questions to you, you used the expression "first lines." Do you recall this?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. When you talk of "first lines," Witness, do you mean by this that there was a subdivision in the organisation of the defence in general, according to which there would have been first lines, for instance, of the BiH army, and then, behind, would there be a second system within the defence lines? Do you know if anything like this existed?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware. And no, there was only one line, Partizanskih Brigada, I am aware and know, and for the rest, it was the Civil Defence that took care of all the fires and everything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. But when you talk about the Civil Defence, the same Civil Defence, did they also organise a defence line in the larger sense of the word?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. Witness, the Civil Defence, did they undergo in any way possible -- were they under the control of an army?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Partly, yes, in some cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Then can you please elaborate, since you know better than anybody else, what the case was.

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In case of injured people and in case of when the injured people had to be carried away, whether it's civilians, women, children, and also soldiers, of course, in case of fires, floods -- but we didn't have any floods thank God -- because for four years we had no electricity and no water. We had to dig wells. But the order would get to us from the command post, and we would have to wake up either in the middle of the night or during the day to evacuate the population. We had to give assistance to everybody independently of whom it was. It was not important who the person was, whether Serbian, Croatian, or a Muslim or whatever the case may be. I cannot remember any more. I was not a nationalist. I never was. I never will be. But if Hadzic gave me the order to go from Buzdevic Ismet and if they told me to go at midnight to go help somebody, either to carry the wounded or anything like that, I had to go. And frankly, I don't want to hide anything from you, you know, that was the war, and it was the army that directed everything, that they take control, and the general knows that very well. We had to obey. The sanctions were like that; the rules, the laws had not changed. It was the laws of Bosnia and Herzegovina, if you do not answer the mobilisation call, you know what awaits you. So you know what happens to you. If you don't want to go, you know you'll have to go to prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You could even get a bullet.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, are you telling me that civilians, such as yourself, had to obey instructions and orders coming from the army, and you could even get punished, and you could even get capital punishment, if I understand correctly? Is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were coming -- the commander of the Civil Defence and the commander of the Civil Defence of Dobrinja, of Novi Grad, actually, he knew -- he had his own orders. He had to carry out the orders, and I do not have the order, I didn't bring it. I didn't bring all the orders, but we had received, for instance, the orders to dig a well for the civilians because the inhabitants were thirsty for two months. I dug a tunnel of ten and a half metres. We had to put pumps in order to supply water to the inhabitants, to the women and children. And there were three pumps. Once we were digging and seven men died. Twenty and some men were wounded during the digging of this well. Maybe you don't know this but they were wounded because a shell fell.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, thank you for these very useful precisions and details, but I would like to know something: When the army needed to get help in terms of supply, would you bring your supplies to the army, material?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I will tell you very honestly to you and to all of you here, Dobrinja was closed off from all sides. And in Butmir, UNPROFOR was in Butmir. And the UNPROFOR did not allow us to go on the other side of the pista with transporters. So this is why we received the order to dig a 10-metre deep -- 10-metre long tunnel, and the order from the Civil Defence arrived, and that was from the Supreme Command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Just a clarification. I have it here in the translation that the UNPROFOR did not allow us to go on the other side of the pista, P-I-S-T-A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I understood. If I'm wrong, I understood the pista to be the runway from the airport.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: It's the airport runway, note of the interpreter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes, it was clear, in fact. Thank you for this answer, Witness. I will now submit to you a document --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Allow me a few minutes to consult my colleague, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I see that you have your glasses on. Do you hear me?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Are you able, Witness, to read with these glasses? Are those reading glasses? It is not an irrelevant question, but we've seen that some witnesses were not able to read certain documents so this is why I'm asking you. Witness, are you able to read with those glasses? Are those reading glasses?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you for your answer. I would like to submit to you a document, with the help of the usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And if the Chamber allows me, Mr. President, with your leave, I would submit these documents to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Leave is granted.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And of course, we have already distributed these documents to the booths, the interpretation booths, therefore, they will help us in interpreting; and we've also given these documents to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, we received copies of these documents which are in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we have them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And they are marked Exhibit D85. We have not received translations of these documents in any of the languages of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I was talking about a document coming -- stemming from the Prosecution, 0205-6659. I thought that they knew what this was about. Because if they didn't know what the contents of these documents were, why did they communicate these documents to us? I thought they already had the translation of these documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I think that the Prosecution is under an obligation to provide -- to give you access to certain documents. Even if they're not translated, the obligation goes further than only translated documents, but apart from that, whatever you tell us about what you expect from the Prosecution, the Chamber has not produced these documents and cannot read it without translation. So it's not just the Prosecution but also the Chamber who would like to have access to the contents of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this is the reason why I asked the witness if he was able to read with his glasses, because what we wish to do is to communicate, to show the copies of this text to everybody, and then I wanted to ask the witness to read out loud the passages that I was going to indicate to him and then I was going to ask the interpreters to interpret these lines for the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, of course, the context of the document, of course, might get lost in this way. But I'd suggest that we first hear what part you'll ask the witness to read.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, do you have before you a document? Witness, I'm talking to you. Witness, do you hear me?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you see --

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you have before you a document?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I do, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: In Serbian.

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and in Bosnian, and in Montenegrin also. Yes, I do have the document before me. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Witness. I would like to ask you the following. If you could tell us if on the left upper hand corner, do we see the reference to the command of the 5th Motorised Brigade in Dobrinja? What do you see?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Left, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well, thank you. Witness, under "Subject" or in Serbian, "Predmet," do you see -- what do you read next to the "Subject," "Predmet," so that we know what the document is about?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I will. It is the regulation of the positions in the second defence line.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. We see the word "Subject," and you have a full column. And can you read us -- read to us what you see.

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Regulation of the positions in the second defence line."

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very good. We are, therefore, talking about a second defence line, line of defence. I would like you to -- ask you to read out loud Item 1, and it is the number 1 that's under the word "Naredjujem" that's right in the middle of the document. So could you please read us Item 1, please.

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You want me to read it. "According to the order given by the Chief of Staff of the 1st Corps, under number 12642, up until today, according to what we have established in order to carry out the work the best possible way."

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Just a little further down.

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This relates to the second and the third motorised brigade but it has nothing to do with the 5th Motorised Brigade. You can read underneath these commanders and all the other ones are not even in Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with you. I fully agree with you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Fazlic.

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It has nothing to do with this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Fazlic, would you please, if you're able to read the lines Defence counsel is asking you to read, would you please do so. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, could you indicate precisely, do you want the witness to read the whole first paragraph or just a few lines?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will tell him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, if you hear me correctly, I would like to ask you to read another passage under the one you just read. It starts with "one." The first word of this passage is "izvrsiti." Do you see this paragraph?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under 1, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Can you read this passage up until the word "battalion."

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. "To regulate the additional regulation of the positions with the construction of installations with concrete profiles with a very light cover; to carry out --" The second: "To carry out works in the second line for the unit that is engaged, and this in order to carry out the works only in order to employ the men from the battalion."

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: All right. Now, I would like to ask you to read the point 2 (a), (b), and the sentence that follows (b), or that is to say "za izvodenje" and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Works on fortification to be carried out as follows: (a) continue fortification of positions on the first line of defence. For the regulation of the second line of defence, engage labour force according to the following timetable: For the execution of works in the area of responsibility of the 1st Motorised Brigade --" please note it's the 1st not the 5th -- "engage 20 men with four pickaxes and six shovels divided into two groups." The 1st Motorised Brigade is quite a different brigade to the one in Dobrinja. Please take note of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Fazlic, we should make a clear distinction from what you read and your comment. If you are asked to read a few lines, please do so, then pause, and if there's any reason to comment on what you've read, then you might do it as part of your answer to a question. But you'll understand that we would like to know exactly what is your reading and what is your opinion given in relation to what you've read. Yes. Please. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I'm not quite sure of the comments you made regarding the brigade, so will you just continue the reading. Will you please now read the sentence beginning with, "The second group..." "Druga grupa..." which is to be found in the middle of the page.

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could you read that sentence, please, up to the third dash, third paragraph. I will stop you when necessary.

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The second group, consisting of ten men with two pickaxes and three shovels should report to Dzenanovic Midhat, Dzani, in the headquarters of the third company in Jawaharlal Nehru Street on the 21st of March, 1993, at 8.30 hours."

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Please continue. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "For the execution of works in the area of responsibility of the 2nd Motorised Brigade, 20 men should be engaged with six pickaxes and eight shovels. The unit with the tools should report on the 21st of March, 1993, at 8.45 hours to commander Handzic Muhamed in B. Mitrova Street, number 1."

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I'm interrupting you. When you see the words, "MTB," just read out "MTB." It could be a battalion and not necessarily a brigade. Every time you see "MTB," just read it as it stands. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "For the execution of works in the area of responsibility of the 3rd MTB, 20 men should be engaged five pickaxes and eight shovels. The unit with its tools should report on the 21st of March, 1993, at 8.30 hours to Simunovic Mirko in Marx and Engels, number 13, square C5."

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: A little more, please.

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "For the execution of works in the area of responsibility of the 4th MTB, 30 men should be engaged with eight pickaxes and ten shovels. The unit, together with its tools, should report to Commander Softic Salko on the 21st of March, 1993, at 8.30 hours in the battalion headquarters. The labour force, together with tools, will be placed at the disposal of Commander Salko Softic."

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. We see that these are instructions given by the command of the 5th Motorised Brigade to people in charge of Civil Defence to report at a certain time and at a certain place, to the headquarters of the battalions. Do you know, Witness, where these headquarters were of the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, and 4th battalion of the 5th Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I just know of the 1st, of the 1st battalion. It was in the shelter, in the atomic shelter on the square called the "Children of Dobrinja." I know that. I don't know about the others. It was a military secret, so I'm not familiar.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for your answers, Witness. Would you agree with me in saying that the Civil Defence lent a helping hand to the army for the construction of military structures on what is known as the first line?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. I take note of your answer. Witness, is it correct to say that the document that you have just read refers to the second line of defence?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, now that we see that there was a system of double defence lines, the first and the second, and that for the second it was the Civil Defence that took charge of it, can you remember now what were those second defence lines?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: These questions are being prefaced with comments by my friend. There was a comment earlier about us seeing that these are instructions given to people in charge of the Civil Defence. Perhaps it is because I don't have a translation where I don't know if that is something which is established, but these are comments which are not part of cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, when Mr. Stamp got up, I was trying to find exactly in my transcript where - and I was just at the point of asking you to assist me - where part of the translated text says that this is -- these are instructions to those in charge of the civilian defence. I might have missed it. But could you please guide me. You can read it. That's one of the problems, that we have no translation at this very moment. But from those parts read out loudly, could you please indicate where in the translation it clearly indicates? I might have missed it. Perhaps you first indicate in the original -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that you have an abbreviation, "CZ." Let me ask the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, if you would please first indicate now, I see a letter "CZ" in the first paragraph, third line, approximately in the middle. Let me just see now what the witness has read is what exactly was the translation. One moment, please. Perhaps you could assist me, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, where exactly this part is translated, where we find it in the transcript in the English language.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will find it in a moment, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it at 60/11, where it starts "To regulate the additional regulation..." I think it's at page 60, line 11, and in the translation it doesn't say anything at all about Civil Defence. So therefore, could you please indicate to the -- to me which words, since you understand the language and since I assume that the witness has read this first paragraph, where the Civil Defence is mentioned? Is that the abbreviation "CZ"?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. The abbreviation "CZ" stands for --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just ask the interpreters. Could the interpreters give a translation of what they would understand "CZ" means.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: If the interpreters may be of assistance, the witness was confused, and he read the paragraph above first, and that's what caused some confusion for the interpreter. But CZ stands for Civil Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do the interpreters have the document in front of them?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would it be able that you translate the second sentence of paragraph 1, which starts with the characters "ZA," --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we have a translation of that specific sentence.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "For the execution of works along the second line of defence, engage exclusively units of the Civil Defence, and for works on the first line, engage exclusively personnel from the units of the battalion."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I think now -- just assuming that the witness intended to read the first paragraph, that at least we now know what the text in it is in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So Mr. Piletta-Zanin, please proceed. But I think we are approximately at the point where we -- yes. Perhaps we first have a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know whether Mr. Stamp's objection is upheld. Does he still have an objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: It was for clarification, and thanks to the Bench, it has been clarified. The --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a perfect moment for the break, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... time, would you need, Mr. Piletta-Zanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't dare make an estimate because -- but Ms. Pilipovic tells me 15 minutes, and I will do my best to respect that time limit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think we would have gained a lot of time if we would have had a translation. It is far more efficient. But let's have a break until 1.00 and save three more minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I will wait for the witness to put his headphones on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Thank you for being here again. I would like to clarify one point. You have answered, and nobody contradicted you in this courtroom, in answer to a question put to you by the Prosecution, you said that there was an incident which involved eight dead people, and at one point 16 people died. For the first quote, it was 3/19, and the second one was 5/07, line and pages. Would you please clarify, because clarity is our goal, how many people died, according to you, in this incident? Maybe you didn't understand me quite clearly. You have a transcript before you. This transcript took down your words. Once you talked about eight people dead, and the other time you talked about 16 people who were killed. I would like to know how many people died, according to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, wouldn't it be better to ask first whether the witness did speak about one or two different occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that he talked about one same incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: But how many incidents did you talk to?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do understand. And I did understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So you do understand?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was talking about one incident, and it was the incident that took place during the football match when the first shell landed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was at the football match.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Well, I understood you clearly, then. We are talking about one incident, but the transcript at one point mentions that eight people were killed and on another occasion that 16 people had been killed or died. Since this is not the same figure, I would like to ask you, according to you, how many people died in this incident?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said when the shell landed, and after I opened my eyes, because I closed my eyes at first, then I opened my eyes, and I saw eight men on the asphalt. They were no longer moving. They had died on the spot, whereas for the others, there were young men, running towards their homes. They went to the hospital so their wounds could be dressed. Some people fell. Alija Gojak was hit here. He just fell two or three seconds after. He left the parking lot but then he fell down to the ground and he died right there. So eight people were in front of me and they were already dead. With regards to the number of people who died pursuant to this incident, was 16 people altogether. Some people died at the hospital, some people died on the spot, so do you understand me now?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So on the spot, at the very same moment people were dismembered. There were eight men dismembered, Dragan, Damir Trebo, Marko, and the others. Whereas for the others, they tried to run across the lawn to go home, or to go to the hospital. And they would just run and fall down, and some were losing blood, and I thought also that I would die right there and then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Fazlic, you perfectly clarified the issue. You explained what the numbers were. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I will come back to this question later; however, I would like to move on to something else. Earlier we talk about the military police and the army. Do you know if at the time of the event or the events, I'm talking about the summer of 1993, were there oppositions between -- important oppositions between the various factions within the area that we sometimes call the "Muslim area" within Sarajevo, inside Sarajevo? Were there dissenting factions, for instance, between the military police, between the army, and between eventually some paramilitary formations?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: My question was probably too long. I will reiterate my question. Sir, to your knowledge, were there any opposing opinions that could have happened during the summer of 1993 from, on the one hand, the army in Dobrinja, the 5th Brigade, and on the other hand, the military police for which you said that you knew their commander?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So you don't know. Very well, thank you, Witness. I will now go back to the second line.

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you, thank you. Now let us talk about this second line. We saw before the break that there was also a second defence line on which or for which the Civil Defence cooperated. What do you know, as a specialist in the Civil Defence matters, what can you tell us about the second defence line?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do know matters related to Civil Defence, but everything that is written here coming from the 5th Motorised Brigade, and it is directed towards the commanders to the Civil Defence, all these orders were also probably directed towards the commanders of various battalions and I don't know who else. I don't know this precisely. I was completely on the other side. I had nothing to do with what you're asking me. This is Vojnicko Polje, Dobrinja V, Nedzarici, C4 as well, whereas I was in another -- I was in IIIB, that side of Dobrinja, in that quadrant, and I was within the civilian defence of Dobrinja IIIB.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for this answer. Thank you. Witness, I believe that you were told to take a weapon since you told us that on two occasions you refused to be drafted, to carry a weapon. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer.

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I just add something, please? May I, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think Mr. Piletta-Zanin will put some additional questions to it, so just wait what Mr. Piletta-Zanin would like to ask you about it. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes, Witness. You said that you refused to carry weapons on two occasions, or to participate in military activities. How old were you when you were asked to carry a weapon, to be drafted?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was approximately 46 years old, because I was born on the 7th of March.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: What was the sanction that you could get if you did not -- if you refused to carry a weapon?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The law that was at the time, the JNA laws that existed in the former Yugoslavia, those laws were also in Bosnia and Herzegovina, because new laws were not promulgated and Bosnia and Herzegovina abided by those rules and by the laws of the army. So if you were mobilised, if you were drafted --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes, but what were the sanctions?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know the law. Maybe you go to jail for a month or two. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Let us now go back to more technical questions. If you know, say yes; if you don't know, say no, and we will thank you for this if you can be brief. Do you know if the 5th Brigade had a mortar battalion within itself which was actually called the 2nd battalion?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps towards the end of 1994, in 1994, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: At the time of the events, was there a battalion, a mortar battalion formed within the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Dobrinja, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So in Dobrinja --

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Dobrinja, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would like to submit to the witness Document D25. It is also -- it had been submitted at the time. I have a copy. I don't know if I should give you our copy. I don't know if you wish to use --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to say that this document has two pages of a translation, sort of a free translation, draft translation, but we would like to show the witness this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would have an additional copy for the Bench to... Of course we can --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do not believe that I have one, but I will hand you my copy. I do know this document very well. I shall ask the question from memory, and I would like to get the document back. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the interpreters also get a copy of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, take the document in the Serbian language that you have before you, please. Are you holding this document, Witness, in the Serbian language?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Would you please go to page number 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: May I just be furnished with a copy of that document.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the interpreters also have one.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just said that I only have one copy. I may leave and get photocopies, if you will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just as the Prosecution indicates, prior to the examination of a witness, what documents they will use, couldn't perhaps at least not later than at the beginning of the cross-examination, the Defence indicate to the Prosecution what they should be prepared for as far as documents are concerned, because it's a bit inefficient this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, certainly. I agree with you, Mr. President. We have discovered this question, this question arose not long ago, while I was consulting Ms. Pilipovic, and you know that, unfortunately, it is very difficult to go and get documents in this building --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course I do understand that you did your utmost best. If it has been before the break, if you said I only intended that this would be a useful document after the break, even during the break, you could say, please be prepared for D25, so that in one or two minutes the Prosecution can retrieve D25. I think that would be better than to give long explanations on how difficult it is. Please proceed, Mr. -- Of course, Mr. Stamp, what are we going to do now?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you allow me, I will go outside and make photocopies. It will not take very long. It will last three minutes, and I will distribute this document or be introduit [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course I would have preferred this to be done during the break and not to interrupt the examination of the witness for this reason.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But Ms. Pilipovic can go and make the photocopies. But she will need your document, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you have any other questions to the witness, perhaps put them first and then we'll come back to D25. Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I shall do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I would like us now to go back to the football match, this event you're talking to us about. Could you please set the document aside, please. Can you hear me? Very well. Thank you. Regarding this football match, Witness, we understood that there were some military targets on one side of the parking lot, but I'm not sure if I understand correctly the distance that existed between the military lines and the end of the football pitch. Could you tell us what the distance was?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I have it here that my friend is saying that "We understood that there were some military targets on one side of the parking lot." This is a comment, and again I'm not sure my friend should be allowed to make comments at this stage of the case. However, I'm not sure also that this comment is warranted by the evidence. I cannot say "We understand or understood" that there were some military targets on one side of the parking lot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You would say that is an interpretation of the words of the witness. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, could you please indicate what exactly you're referring to. It's not my recollection, but I might be mistaken that the witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, gladly. 30/23, Mr. President. I'm referring to 30/23 on my computer, but my computer is letting me down. But anyway, it is line 30/23 when the witness was talking about the first lines. In my handwritten notes, I see 30/23.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: On 30/23, I read that the witness said: "As far as the first lines and the soldiers on duty in the first lines are concerned..." I'm just trying to find where we exactly have the part of your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're talking about my question, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. What you said is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was talking about military targets, because the witness himself spoke about the first lines and the soldiers who were on duty on those first lines. He said nothing more than that, but he did mention that. For the Defence, the first lines are a military target, and soldiers on duty are equally military targets. And that is why I wanted to shorten things --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Just for clarification, the objection is to the comment made prefacing the question where my friend said, "We --" and I don't know who he is referring to when he says, "we," but he said, "We understood that there are military targets on one side of the parking lot." Not line, he was speaking about parking lot, and he was speaking about something that "we," whoever that is, understood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, if you'd like to refer to an earlier answer of the witness, would you please do it by referring to his words. So if you say, "You told that the first lines were..." and then I wonder what would then come, were they at one side of the parking lot or were they outside the parking lot at one side and at what distance? But if you refer to an earlier answer, you should do it as precise as possible. So rephrase your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, when I say "we," it is out of politeness. In France, I think we all understand that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm not mainly referring to -- we understand that -- I do understand what you mean by that, perhaps that's part of the French eloquency, but my major point was that you're referring -- the witness spoke about first lines, and you're talking about military targets. That is not the same, although you might interpret first lines to be military targets. But that's not what the witness said. If you refer to what the witness said, you do it in the words he used. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Quite. So I use the term "military targets" implying first line and soldiers on duty. For the Defence, these are military targets. But let me put my question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... is to explain why your conclusions were right. I want you to refrain from any further comment. If I say, "Please rephrase your question," you may rephrase the question. You may not explain to us why you were perfectly right to put the question in the way you did it. So would you please, I repeat it, rephrase your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, did you speak about the first lines, please? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For heaven's sake, I told you. I marked them on the map, and there were no other lines behind them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Fazlic, it's perfectly clear you confirmed three times that you used the word "first lines." So the question has already been answered. Would you please put your next question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, these defence lines, Witness, at what distance were they from the far end of this parking lot, roughly, approximately?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, can you add up. You add up, and then you can work it out what the distance is from the parking lot to the army that held the lines.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Fazlic, Mr. Fazlic, Mr. Fazlic, the question was whether you could tell us how far the first lines you spoke about were away from the end of the parking lot, what was the distance, approximately. If you say --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I be given a little time, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] About 210, 215 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer, sir. I should now like you to look at the document that you have in front of you. Will you please take the Serbian version, the one written in the Serbian language. I think that everyone has copies of the draft translation and the original text.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Unfortunately, the interpreters do not have the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, could you please look at the second page of that document. Will you please look at the second page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you do it slowly because the interpreters have not yet received the translation, so we have some difficulty. But please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, will you look at the second page. That's it. You have it. That's fine. Witness, will you please read -- please read -- sorry -- point F of page 2 of this document.

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: F, you said. Under 1, paragraph F: "Casualties in personnel and materiel are unknown to us."

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Which document are you looking at, sir?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first document. The first page.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you have a second page, Witness, please? Beginning with the paragraph F. F. Do you have it, the second page?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's the first line of the second page.

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The wounded." Is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Read it, please. Read this paragraph, please.

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The combatants of two MTB mortar company of 120/82 millimeters, Jamakovic Rasid and Jasar Jasminko are wounded. Six combatants are killed and 55 are wounded as a result of two mortar shells of 82 millimetres which fell on a parking lot where a football match was held and where there was a number of spectators. At this event, five civilians were killed and 32 persons wounded. These data --"

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You can stop there, please. Witness, would you agree with me --

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Just wait a minute, please. Wait a minute. Just a moment, please. Please. Wait for me to phrase my question, and then answer it. Witness, would you agree with me in saying that, according to this document, there were soldiers who were wounded and who belonged to a mortar company of 120 82-millimetre?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Why, Witness, do you not agree with that?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because those men were not playing the match. They were passing by. They were spectators, and they were wounded outside the pitch, on the parking lot. No, on the road or somewhere else, anywhere else, those two men, you see. 16 people were killed and 82 were wounded. So this report is not correct, and I don't agree with it. You can check out the names. They can be found in the Centar, or rather, Novi Grad municipality, and you will see who was wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I'm interrupting you. This document, will you read who signed it, please. Can you read it.

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Anyone could have signed it. I don't care.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Since you're saying that anyone could sign it, will you please read out the name that it says here.

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. Ismet Hadzic. All I know is --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: What is the word that you read above the name Ismet Hadzic?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Commander."

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: What is the stamp that you see under the signature of Ismet Hadzic?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Motorised Brigade."

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And the number before the word "Motorised Brigade"?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose it's number 5, 5th.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, it is the stamp of the 5th Motorised Brigade. So Witness, do you know whether 55 soldiers were wounded in this attack?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment. May I confer with my colleague for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, do you know as when Territorial Defence was set up in Dobrinja and the area known as the airport?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: If I tell you the 6th of May, 1992, does that appear to be acceptable?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you know, Witness, when the 1st battalion of Dobrinja was formed, in May 1992?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. These were secrets that we didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Do you know whether on the 6th of July, 1992, that the 1st Dobrinja Brigade was formed, which later became the 5th Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether those dates are correct, I don't know. I have no idea. I don't know when which brigade was formed. All I know is that on the 23rd of June, I was called to the shelter to be mobilised. On the 23rd of June, 1992, I was called to the shelter for mobilisation. And when what was established, founded, drafted, I don't know. I'm an ordinary citizen who had no access to such information so don't ask me about them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No further questions, Mr. President. Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Mr. Stamp, is there any need to re-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: There is no need to re-examine the witness, Mr. President. But if I may ask your permission to ask the interpreters' booth to have a look at the document which the witness was just presented with and to interpret it for us, for the record. Because I think when he spoke, he was going very quickly with the reading of a particular passage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you have a particular passage in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: On the B/C/S version, it would be the sentence at 2(e), and the sentence at 2(f).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 2(e) and 2(f). First of all, what document are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That is the document D25, which was last --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I was confused. I thought you were talking about D85. D25, we have an English translation of D25.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I beg your pardon, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D25, we were provided with a translation in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes. And in respect to what I heard when 2(f) was read and translated, there is a small area which seems to be missing from the translation which was read onto the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You'd say that it's not on the record now; it's on paper but not on the record. Could you please indicate, then, which part it was. Would the parties agree that the translation of this document is to start with a reliable translation? And could you please tell us which part is missing? Because...

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The translation of what the witness was asked to read at 2(f) seems to have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you indicate on what line, what page.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: In the B/C/S version --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I mean in the transcript. 78. Yes. Yes, I see that on 78 line 23, the witness starts reading. The last part seems not to have been --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: "These data..." and there are some lines --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You mean if the witness has read 2(f), then it reads, at least in the translation, "These data are unofficial," and I think as a matter of fact Mr. Piletta-Zanin then interrupted the witness and said that he didn't have to read any further, where it reads on paper, "These data are unofficial. All detailed information regarding these events will be submitted by a security officer." Is that the part you --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can we just -- yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is I indeed did stop the witness there, but we could have lost a lot of time. But there's no problem. We can have the witness read the whole --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would the parties agree that the last line of 2(f) read by the witness was -- are the words I just pronounced? If so, then --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: It is agreed, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You agree as well, Mr. Piletta-Zanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is absolutely correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Does that solve the problem, Mr. Stamp?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No further questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Are there any further questions from my colleagues?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Yes, I have a question for Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it prior to additional questions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: No, no, no, it's just a clarification on the translation. My question is, Mr. Piletta-Zanin: [Interpretation] You used, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you used the word "free translation." What is that?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me. The expression "free translation" usually means a translation that was not done by a sworn translator, not by someone like those here who have taken an oath. Therefore, this free translation doesn't have the same sacred quality as would have a translation by a sworn translator.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Fazlic, Judge El Mahdi has one or more questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like you to tell me, please, you said during your testimony that before and after the date of the incident on the 1st of June, there was shelling. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And each time that there was shelling, was there just one or several shells that were fired in a line, one after another, consecutively?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were three or four one after another, and then they would switch to another side, and after, there would be an infantry attack by the infantry, the troops, the soldiers. So first there would be shelling, exclusively with mortars from Dobrinja IV, the Trappara [phoen] houses, the barracks, this would last about half an hour, and after a half hour of shelling --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you. But if you remember, how much time would go by between the impact of one shell and the next one?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be 10 to 15 metres [as interpreted] between shells that would fall in a series of three, four, or five. And these would fall in the parking lot. Yes, in the parking lot, others on the grassy surface, but those that fell on the parking lot were more dangerous than those on the grass.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I see, but the condition of the parking, was it suitable to be used as a football pitch in view of all the impacts of mortar shells on it?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As we were closed on all sides, we turned that parking lot into a rubbish dump. We would bring rubbish there and burn it during the night.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but the holes provoked by the shelling, didn't this bother the players? Could you still play football on such a pitch?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. No, never. Never again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Fazlic. I've also a question for you. You told us that you refused to carry any arms when you were asked to do so.

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you tell me, who asked you to carry arms?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you: The command and the Presidency proclaimed a mobilisation, a state of war. And according to the law enforced at the time, all able-bodied men fit for the army had to report to their military assignment, to their units to which they were assigned. I did not have an assignment because I had been in the reserve in the police force as a reserve traffic policeman for many years. I had performed my duties. I took off my uniform. However, up to the age of 65, you were obliged to report to the command, and I reported to the command exactly on the 23rd of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then you told them that you would not carry any arms?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I told them to their face. I never killed anyone; I won't kill anyone now, and I refuse to take up a weapon. I'll do anything, I'll do whatever is necessary; I'll dig trenches. But for me to shoot at a child carried by his mother, a child of 5 or 6, I would never do that. And I'm telling you all, quite frankly, I'm that kind of a person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This was your answer to a general order to come and join the Defence Forces, at least, the armed forces, yes. Thank you very much for your answer. Mr. Fazlic, you've answered all our questions by now. That means that this concludes your testimony in this Court. I have been aware that you would have told us for many more hours on all your experiences, but in this Court, the rules are that you have to answer the questions put to you by the parties and by the Judges. And I thank you very much for having answered these questions. I know it's quite a journey to come to The Hague --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I say something, Your Honour, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you may say something but it depends on what whether I'll allow you to --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I won't insult anyone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course not. I don't expect you to do so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You see, I'm a man who worked for 30 years honestly. I had everything. I was wounded, and I'm 70 per cent disabled. My wife was wounded 100 per cent, and my son 100 per cent. Three, three of us. And I'm in a wheelchair. Up to you to judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course, we noticed that you and your family are bearing consequences of the events at that time, and I think this Bench is fully aware.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not to blame. I'm not guilty. I didn't ask for the war. I didn't ask for the war. I didn't conduct the war. I didn't want it, nor did my family. I did an honest man's work, and I reached a point when I can't move around. Now why? Why? I'm not insulting anyone, because on the other side, there were similar incidents. I do apologise for saying this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Fazlic, you expressed to us that as an honest man, you nevertheless became a victim of a war.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have all the documents, if you need them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We don't need your documents, but don't think that this Court is not aware of what wars can create --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you all, and I had a lot of trouble to come here. Sarajevo, The Hague, you can imagine the transportation and everything, how hard it was for me, being an invalid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Especially in your circumstances, I thank you once again very much for coming, and I wish you a safe trip home again. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, too. Thank you for working so well to punish those who are to blame. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you please escort Mr. Fazlic out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's then deal with the documents tendered in evidence. Madam Registrar, could you please guide us. Madam Registrar asked me what to do when we came to D85. I said to stop for a moment and we'll see what we're going to do

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P3678A, 360-degree Quicktime movie. Exhibit P3281B, video. Exhibit P1197, letter of discharge in B/C/S. P1197.1, English translation. D84, map marked by witness. And then we have D85.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let me first give a decision -- yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, just to help matters, if somebody asked us here, we would gladly furnish once again a rough translation of this document, if it may help the Prosecution. This is, of course, in view of the search of truth, and we would do it gladly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The problem is that if various parts of this document are to be used by the Defence and if it is to be taken in context, we need a proper translation. We understand the difficulty with the huge amounts of documents in B/C/S, but the official languages of the Court are French and English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, yes, I would gladly do so. I must say that one of the reasons for which it was not possible to do so, it is because, as I already said, we studied, up until late last night, documents that were supposed to be given to us by the Prosecution, or submitted by the Prosecution but which were, in extremis, withdrawn from our sight and from you. And unfortunately, the time cannot be invented. We can always find time but it is not invented. So we shall do these translations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The document which is tendered as D85 has been disclosed by the Prosecution to the Defence, and no one can require, especially not if a reciprocal disclosure obligation exists, no one can require the Prosecution to give an English translation of documents disclosed under this obligation.
