So that's the first step. It has been provided to the Defence in the original language. If the Defence wants to tender a document in B/C/S in evidence, they should provide a translation. They have objected, and we have taken these objections very seriously, that the Prosecution sometimes has used translations which were not beyond any doubt as far as their position was concerned, and we ordered that a proper translation should be made. Similarly, the Defence will have to provide a translation of the document before we will admit the document in evidence. And if on the basis of the context of this document, the Prosecution would see a necessity to recall the witness, of course then opportunity will be given to the Prosecution to do so. So therefore, D85 will not at this moment be admitted into evidence, but as we have had at earlier occasions a procedure where we would postpone a final decision on the admission in evidence until a translation had been provided, a similar thing will be done in relation to this document. Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Just to make it clear, we have no objection to the document being received in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I think all that is required is to get an official translation of the document. It is not a difficult thing, and we would not object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We took a similar decision that we would not admit into evidence documents where there was no proper translation, so we'll do exactly the same for the Defence. So even if you would not object, this Court, if we would admit it in evidence and if there's no translation ever given to us, then it is admitted into evidence and we would have to reverse our decision upon the translation not being provided in due time. So I would do exactly the same as we did to the Prosecution. Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, I just wanted to let you know that tomorrow this Chamber will receive the draft translation. This is the first point. Second point, we still do not know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, let me say, we want a translation; we do not want a draft and then a final version. We want a translation and we will then finally decide on the admission into evidence. I don't know how far the Defence can rely on any translation services provided by the Registry. I'm not fully aware if at all within your budget that you could provide us with a proper translation, but we'll have one translation. If it's there, it can be checked by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: My understanding is insofar as documents intended to be put before the Court, they are equally entitled to engage the services of the Registry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That was what my impression was as well. So I see Ms. Pilipovic nodding no. Let's give it a test. Let's see whether this document can be translated. The Chamber insists on having a proper translation. So let's give it a try and see what happens and report to the Chamber if your request will be refused.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We shall see, gladly, Mr. President. And thank you for this. Next point before we do not raise an objection on a document, I would like to ask Mr. Stamp if he could tell us from where was the 360-degree photo was taken. I don't know if Mr. Stamp was following, I don't think so. There are many crosses on the ground. I would like to know, Mr. Stamp, where was this picture taken from, because we will study the testimony of this witness at a later stage, and it was very important for us to know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the testimony has been given by the witness, and I can imagine that in order to avoid unnecessary calling other witnesses, especially the investigators, that perhaps the parties could communicate on this issue. And if there is a problem remaining, then of course we would like to be informed. It might necessitate the -- because usually we have the yellow paint cross, spray paint --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but Mr. President, precisely, that's the point. This could be one of the objections regarding this document. We did not really follow from where was this picture taken, and this is why maybe I was lost. Maybe Mr. Stamp can clarify the point. I will accept his explanation if he may do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, so I do understand that apart from your general objection against 360-degree photographs, you have a specific objection in regard of this photograph because it is not clear from I would say the video or from whatever document, from what position exactly the 360-degree photograph has been taken. And you are willing to reconsider this objection if you are informed by Mr. Stamp about this question. I don't know whether Mr. Stamp could answer immediately or that he would need some time to find out.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If the question is from where the 360-degree photograph was taken, it is from the football pitch -- the parking lot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think that's -- usually we have it precise, on Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the centimetre more or less, that it has been explained to us that if a witness indicates a place where he was, that a yellow cross will be spray painted and from exactly that spot the 360-degrees photograph. As you may understand, a football pitch is -- well, we know exactly how wide it is or long it is by now, at least what the witness told us. So that gives a variety of places where the centre of the 360-degrees photograph could be, and I think that's the problem of Mr. Piletta-Zanin. You could do it at every corner of the football pitch.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed. For the purposes of the -- of that bit of evidence for this shelling incident, I would submit respectfully that it is sufficient in depicting the area of the -- the area within which this incident occurred. If my friend requires to know to precision where exactly on the football pitch this 360-degree photo was taken, I could answer later but my information is that we have called a witness, and we will recall that witness, to explain how these photographs were taken and exactly where they were taken from. I think for the purposes of admissibility, which is the question here, the fact that the witness could identify the photograph and identify what was in the photograph would be sufficient for it to be received into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We are in a situation where there is an objection. We could either decide on the objection right away - we'll not do it then now, but do it by tomorrow morning - but there is an offer of Mr. Piletta-Zanin that he would reconsider his objection if he would receive the information he seeks. If the objection would be withdrawn, we don't have to take a decision. That's our situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's see what we do tomorrow morning first. If you have been communicating with the Defence, and if they indicate to us tomorrow morning that the objection doesn't stand any more --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Maybe I am misunderstanding what is the precise issue here. Does Mr. Piletta-Zanin want to know precisely from where the 360-degree photograph was taken?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that he would like to know if it was from the centre of the pitch or from one of the goals, or from one of the corner flags. That's at least, how I understand it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That information will be transmitted to him in due course for tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and then we'll hear tomorrow morning whether the objection still stands or not, and then, finally, we'll give a decision on the 360-degrees photograph. All the other evidence tendered is admitted, apart, then, from D85.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I do understand that the document used today, D25, was already admitted into evidence at an earlier stage of this trial. So D85, we wait until we have the translation. D25, we wait until tomorrow morning and hear from the parties. I apologise for all those assisting us that it took us until after 2.00, and I see that Mr. Stamp would even continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I just rise to indicate to the Court that insofar as D25 was admitted in evidence along with a draft translation, I shall attempt to assist the Court by providing, as soon as possible, an official translation in respect to D25, if it please the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I see that all the parties are trying to get the best possible translations. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, half a minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We were talking about D85, I believe. But not D25 already admitted. It's just for the clarification of things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think Mr. Stamp offered that, apart from the unsworn translation, that he would seek to provide a sworn translation as soon as possible as well. Is my understanding right, Mr. Stamp?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll really adjourn until tomorrow morning, 9.00, same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 2.08 p.m., to be reconvened on Friday, the 5th day of April, 2002, at 9.00 a.m. 20 21 22 23 24 25
